hajlibc is a C library built from the ground up, in C and a little assembly. It does not sit on top of another libc: it talks to the Linux kernel directly through its own system call layer, brings its own program startup and thread-local storage, and is built freestanding.

Over its releases it has grown from the runtime and the type system to strings and characters, standard I/O streams, number conversion, its own memory allocator (also usable on its own with LD_PRELOAD), POSIX and C11 threads, signals, scheduling, memory mapping and time.

The goal is conformance to POSIX.1-2024. Progress is measured on every release by scanning what the library actually defines against the specification, and behaviour is checked by blåsix, a test suite written from the standards rather than from another libc. Everything below is regenerated from the repository each time the site is built.
